title: Imaging and Surgery Core
text: ABSTRACT – Core B The imaging and surgical core will provide state-of-the-art imaging services to the program. Dr. Randolph’s experience in organizing collaborative teams and her laboratory's background in macrophage biology and lymphatic/vascular trafficking of immune cells and lipoproteins will facilitate applications in imaging that will be tailored to the science of each project. The core will incorporate major contributions from highly expert co- investigators. Dr. Bernd Zinselmeyer is an expert in multiple modalities of light microscopy, including its application in studies of the CNS. He will contribute several lines of expertise in the grant, from confocal and 2- photon microscopy to high-speed epifluorescence imaging. Dr. Song Hu is an innovator in photoacoustic imaging with demonstrated expertise in using this technology to study the vasculature of the CNS. Dr. Igor Smirnov is an expert microsurgeon who will provide and oversee highly skilled surgical manipulations for the projects, including procedures like skull transplant and skull thinning. These co-investigators bring more than their state-of-the-art expertise; they also all bring demonstrated collaborations with one or more project leaders. By working together, this core team of investigators and affiliated staff will offer to all projects the following range of expert surgical procedures and imaging applications. The aims of the imaging and surgical core are to (1) carry out deep-tissue imaging of meninges and outer regions of the brain, (2) apply combinatorial methods (2-photon, high-speed widefield, and photoacoustic imaging) for intravital imaging to investigate macrophage behavior and blood flow dynamics in the meninges, and (3) employ established and novel tools to quantify molecular outflow from the meningeal space.

title: Optic-nerve-head (ONH) Chips for Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration
text:
The most prominent causative risk factor of glaucoma, the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, is
elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), which could deform the optic nerve head (ONH) and cause glaucomatous
neurodegeneration. However, current glaucoma therapies that focus on lowering IOP do not stop vision loss
effectively, and thus there is a pressing need to understand the mechanisms underlying glaucoma
pathogenesis. In this project, we will develop a biomimetic ONH-on-a-chip system that closely mimics the key
anatomic and pathophysiological characteristics of the native ONH to study astrocytic mechanisms of
glaucoma pathogenesis, a missing link to develop efficacious therapies.

title: Quantifying the Integrity of Sleep-Dependent Memory Processing in Pathological Aging and Alzheimer's Disease: Toward Inexpensive Electroencephalographic Wearable Applications
text:
Simple single-channel electroencephalography (EEG) sleep recordings contain information about memory
circuits that may form the basis of a digital biomarker for monitoring brain health and for the detection of early
Alzheimer's disease changes. Our team has pioneered novel methods to measure sleep's memory circuits from
sleep EEG, and we have observed striking changes in these circuits with aging and in the early stages of
Alzheimer's disease. Here, we propose to incorporate our signal processing methods into cutting-edge machine
learning models with the goal to develop predictive models that can serve as a powerful digital biomarker to
detect pathological aging, predict cognitive decline, and detect early stages of Alzheimer's disease.

title: Dedicated breast PET and MRI for characterization of breast cancer and its response to therapy
text:
This proposal aims to address clinical needs where current imaging methods face challenges and new imaging
methods are pursed, using a novel dedicated breast positron emission tomography. Our research may enable
early evaluation of the effectiveness of pre-surgery endocrine therapy for patients with hormone receptor-positive
HER2-negative breast cancer. Additionally, the diagnosis and pre-surgery assessment of invasive lobular breast
cancer may become more precise compared to the current methods.

title: The biochemical, topological and functional impact of cancer-associated Ctcfmutations and their contribution to cancer
text:
PROJECT 1: NARRATIVE
The CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) is a highly conserved protein that plays a crucial role in organizing chromatin
structure and gene expression. Project 1 will study WT and nine high-frequency cancer-associated CTCF
mutants in the background of distinct transcriptional programs to determine how CTCF-mediated looping
contributes to the control of cis regulatory element (CRE) hubs, regions that encompass multiple genes and
enhancers that co-regulate each other through enhancer-promoter chromatin looping. This study will provide
fundamental insights into the mechanisms of CTCF-mediated chromatin organization and gene regulation in the
context of transcriptional programming, with significant implications for understanding the etiology and treatment
of human diseases, including cancer and developmental disorders.

title: ELAVL1 role in glioblastoma heterogeneity through intercellular gene transfer mediated by cell fusion and tunneling membrane nanotube formation
text:
Project Narrative.
From high-resolution spatial cell transcriptional profiling in glioma tissue slices with intact biological architecture
and direct assessment in vivo to cell-specific targeted gene knockdown in a mimicked glioma microenvironment
in vitro and back to assessments in glioma models in vivo, we propose to characterize mechanisms of cell
fusion/TNT formations as the sources of glioma heterogeneity and intercellular gene transfers. Prognostic
profiles of established and novel biomarkers of cell-fusion/TNT formation in the context of a complex glioma
microenvironment will be established for different glioma subtypes. The HuR-dependent axis in the regulation of
cell fusion/TNT formation at different environmental stress modalities (to include hypoxic, mechanical, metabolic,
and cytotoxic stress) will be explored; the quantitative values of HuR inhibitors, including the newly developed
and recently patented by our group inhibitor of HuR dimerization SRI4212, in the suppression of the cell fusion
and glioma heterogeneity will be provided.

title: The functional roles of TGF-beta signaling in cardiac lymphangiogenesis during myocardial ischemia
text:
Abnormal cardiac lymphatic vessel structure and function are associated with ischemic cardiac diseases
including myocardial infarction (MI). However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms during MI that drive
cardiac lymphatic dysfunction during the disease progression have never been explored. This proposal will
investigate previously unidentified functional roles of TGFβ signaling during MI in regulating cardiac
lymphangiogenesis, with a potential leading to the generation of novel therapeutics to promote functional
lymphatics during cardiovascular disease.

title: Trophic interactions directing proper kidney development
text:
Kidney organogenesis requires extensive cellular crosstalk to enable proper development and the establishment
of physiological function. We have uncovered novel roles for renal vascular and neuronal networks in supporting
organogenesis and our goal is to identify the molecular programs mediating crosstalk between these networks
and with the developing kidney. Our findings will support efforts to regenerate and engineer vascularized,
innervated, and functionally mature kidney tissues.

title: A Neuroecological Approach to Examining the Effects of Early Life Adversity on Adolescent Drug Use Vulnerabilities Using the ABCD Dataset
text:
The proposed project will inform public health research and practice on developing prevention and intervention
programs that will mitigate the effect of adversity on adolescent drug use vulnerability and later drug use and
abuse. In addition, our study will help determine the utility of neuromarkers to advance addiction prevention
models via earlier and more accurate risk assessments.

title: Mechanisms of ciliopathy associated structural birth defects
text:
Ciliopathies are complex genetic disorders that can exhibit severe birth defects due to abnormalities in the
formation or function of the cilium. A large number of proteins are thought to be involved in the cilium, but in only
a few of these do we know the molecular pathways in which they function and whether they are associated with
disease (ciliopathies). In this proposal, we take advantage of the explosion of genomic information from patients
with rare developmental disorders and recent advances in identifying genes associated with the cilium to identify
novel ciliopathies in rare and undiagnosed disease repositories, generate precision engineered mouse models
corresponding to these patients, define the molecular and cellular pathways responsible for their birth defects,
and generate data that can be used to predict therapeutic strategies through CPAM's drug discovery pipeline.

title: Mechanistic studies of the genetic contribution of desmoplakin to pulmonary fibrosis in alveolar type 2 cells
text:
In recent decades, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified genetic variants associated
with a variety of traits and diseases, a critical first step towards understanding the molecular mechanisms
that underlie common health conditions. In many cases, however, the functions of GWAS genes, the
mechanisms and consequences of their dysfunction, or the relevant cell types in which their dysfunction
manifests a clinically significant phenotype remain poorly understood. This application applies a
combination of bioinformatic analysis, human induced pluripotent stem cell modeling, and mouse studies
to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the GWAS gene DSP modulates function of type 2
alveolar epithelial cells and contributes to the pathogenesis of pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Novel Methods for Identifying Genetic Interactions for Cancer Prognosis
text:
Our group has taken a leading role in the development and application of cutting-edge gene-environment
interaction analysis methodologies for cancer prognosis. In this renewal, we will develop a suite of statistically
principled deep learning strategies and methods, effectively and cost-effectively harness information from three
different sources, and fundamentally improve stability and interpretability. Powerful data generated by the Yale
SPORE, VA MVP, and TCGA studies on lung and skin cancers will be analyzed.

title: Novel experimental and machine learning - assisted techniques to assess receptive field functionality in the retina
text:
The proposed research is relevant to NEI mission because it studies fundamental circuit mechanisms that are involved in
visual perception. Our work will provide novel theoretical and empirical approaches to understand neuronal function in
and beyond the retina.

title: Hypothalamic MC4Rs and Antipsychotic Drug-Induced Metabolic Syndrome
text:
We use a multidiscipline approach to study the role of Mc4r in antipsychotic drug (APD)-induced weight
gain. Our studies aim to establish that two widely prescribed APDs target a common hypothalamic pathway to
cause hyperphagia and obesity. The overarching goal is to develop novel mechanism-based therapeutics to
mitigate APD-induced metabolic syndrome in millions of patients.

title: Development of PET Tracer for Imaging Brain Inflammation
text:
Project Narrative. Oxidative imbalance and functional impairment of mitochondria mediates
pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and its related
disorders (ADRDs). Although mitochondria are among the prominent intracellular site for ROS
generation, standard clinical 18F-FDG PET/CT lacks sensitivity and diagnostic robustness. Furthermore,
the mechanism of its retention and trapping poorly correlates with oxidative imbalance. To address this
critical unmet need, this project is focused on biochemical validation of a novel redox-sensitive
molecular PET imaging probe (identified as 18F-SLN-128) in Huntington’s disease and AD transgenic
mice models, GMP production to obtain regulatory approval (eIND from FDA) including institutional
RDRC, IRB approvals, and human dosimetry studies as well as assessment in AD participants for
objective of its translation from the bench into clinical nuclear medicine for healthcare management.
Successful accomplishment of proposed aims could deliver a redox-sensitive PET molecular imaging
agent for stratification of therapeutic choices or alterations in lifestyles for managing ROS-mediated
mitochondrial dysfunction in neurodegenerative diseases in general, and AD and ADRDs in particular.

title: Determining the Unique Molecular and Cellular Features of Limbic-predominant Age-related TDP43 Encephalopathy
text:
TDP-43 proteinopathies are common in the aged population; Limbic-predominant Age-related
TDP-43 Encephalopathy (LATE) affects an estimated 30% of individuals >85 years old. Their
treatment is limited by unreliable ante-mortem diagnosis and the absence of disease-modifying
therapies. By leveraging natural variability in TDP-43 proteinopathies, I aim to identify cellular
and molecular drivers of disease progression, which can inform biomarker and therapy
development.

title: Innovation in Suicide Prevention Research Center (INSPIRE)
text:
The University of Pennsylvania Innovation in Suicide Prevention Research Center (INSPIRE). Suicide is a
leading cause of death in the US especially among adolescents and young adults. Although effective
interventions for youth and young adults exist, they are not widely disseminated, and when used, they are often
not delivered with fidelity over time hampering their impact. To address this problem, the INSPIRE Center’s
overarching goals are to develop and adapt practical suicide prevention interventions for youth and young adults
and to use advanced technologies and implementation strategies to optimize how evidence-based practices can
be brought to scale efficiently, and with high fidelity, for optimal effectiveness. Our work will prioritize strategies
that can be rapidly deployed in acute care and community practice, thereby increasing reach and public health
impact and, thus, INSPIRE is poised to transform for suicide prevention research and practice to address a
pressing public health crisis among the nation’s youth and young adults.

title: Parp Function in Prostate Cancer
text:
Prostate cancer remains the second leading cause of deaths due to cancer in
North American men. Defining the communication pathways that operate within prostate
cancer cells, which is to say, how proteins talk to each other, reveals vulnerabilities that can be
exploited therapeutically. We discovered a communication pathway in prostate cancer cells, and
propose to determine how it works, and if pathway inhibition with a new drug (in clinical trials)
can kill prostate cancer cells.

title: Advanced Brain-Penetrant Enzyme Therapy to Treat Lafora Disease
text:
Lafora disease (LD) is a rare and fatal childhood neurodegenerative disorder that leads to seizures,
Alzheimer’s-like dementia in the teenage years, and death within 10 years of onset. This project brings
together experienced teams at the University of Florida and the Wyss Institute’s Brain Targeting Program at
Harvard Medical School that have developed a novel brain-penetrant therapeutic that clears the toxic brain
polyglucosan bodies (PGBs) responsible for LD. Our proposal is built on past discoveries and the results from
our planned studies are critical for advancing our recently engineered LD therapy from the laboratory to the
clinic.

title: Agonism of Sirtuin 1 Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Tobacco Smoking
text:
Cigarette smoking is a significant health problem within US military. Although the prevalence of smoking has
declined among US adults, there are opportunities to reduce smoking related cardiac dysfunction among US
veterans. This grant pursues to understand how an impaired cardioprotective signaling causes a higher inci-
dence of cardiac dysfunctions in the veterans’ hypertension population with cigarette smoking and has the po-
tential to discover new therapeutic strategies to limit myocardial dysfunction by cigarette smoking in these vet-
erans’ patients.
